entities.summary: James Macfadyen (1799–1850) was a Scottish medical doctor and botanist who made a significant contribution to the scientific study of the plants of the Caribbean region. Born in Glasgow on 3 May 1799, he was the eldest son of a music publisher and bookseller, John Macfadyen, and his wife Elisabeth. Macfadyen was the first to describe the grapefruit scientifically - he gave it its Linnean name, Citrus paradisi - and to describe new species of fig trees and other Caribbean plants. In addition to his botanical work, Macfadyen was a pioneering figure in the field of tropical medicine, and his papers on the subject were widely read and influential. He was also an avid collector of medicinal plants and established a private collection of over 1,000 specimens, which was later acquired by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Macfadyen's work had a lasting impact on the field of botany and tropical medicine, and he is still recognized as a leading figure in the history of Caribbean botany. His discovery of the grapefruit's scientific name has been particularly celebrated, and it remains a testament to his groundbreaking work in the field.
